claims.claim: As read on 2026-09-15, DAZ's EULA section 3.0 "Interactive License Addendum" ("Addendum 3.0") is "in force only when User has purchased a Game Developer License or an Interactive License Add-On ("Interactive License") from the online DAZ store." The two triggers scope differently: an Interactive License Add-On is bought per product and covers only "all Content for which the User has purchased such an Interactive License" (on the store it is a per-item checkbox, e.g. US$50.00 on a US$29.99 prop, non-discountable and non-refundable, and offered only where the product's creator chose to offer one); a Game Developer License is not per product but per Artist Name (the Addendum applies to purchased Content only if the User holds Game Developer Licenses "for each of the Artist Names" on the product, and a "Daz Originals" GDL covers all Content listing "Daz Originals" as an artist). The DAZ store returned no Game Developer License products for sale on 2026-09-15, so in practice the per-product Add-On is what a new buyer can obtain. Under the store's standard terms DAZ states an Interactive License "is required when using or distributing 3D content from the Daz 3D store, whether modified or in its original form, in video games or other applications" (sprites built from stacked renders excepted), and the base licence only grants 2D renderings and forbids distributing anything from which Content "can be separately exported, extracted or de-compiled". It is not the only contractual route: the EULA says a version "signed by both parties" supersedes it, and DAZ's "express written consent" is required (and is the only route) for any discrete in-game sale of the content or its derivatives, and for cloud-based or post-install content distribution by entities with annual revenue over US$1,000,000. The Addendum's key grant, which replaces section 1.0 "Terms of Use" for CRT Content only, is that the User may "incorporate, copy and modify the CRT Content in the creation and presentation of two-dimensional animations and renderings which may require access to the CRT Content by the User's customer during electronic execution of the User's application", provided the CRT Content cannot be "separately exported, extracted, or de-compiled into any re-distributable form or format" and the User ensures it is "not available to end users in their native formats" and protects it "by employing technology, asset protection, encryption or any other resources at User's disposal."

claims.claim: As of 2026-09-15 (DAZ Importer stable 5.2.0, dev source 5.3.0, GitHub wiki last updated 2026-09-11), Diffeomorphic imports Genesis morphs as armature (rig) property sliders with Blender drivers generated from the DSON "formulas" in the .dsf files, driving mesh shape keys and/or bone transforms (Genesis 3/8 face units are bone poses, FACS morphs combine shape keys and bone poses, body morphs drive bones, JCMs and flexions are shape keys driven by bone rotations). The drivers approximate rather than reproduce Daz's formula behaviour: Daz TCB splines are approximated with smoothstep(), a Daz slider that is both driven and dialable is split into raw and final values, and multi-layer driver chains are flattened. Standard morph types selectable in the Morphs panel are Face Units, Expressions, Visemes, FACS Units, FACS Details (Genesis 9 only), FACS Expressions, Body Morphs, JCMs and Flexions, plus Custom Morphs in user-named categories; Easy Import additionally offers Head, Anime, PowerPose, Bulges, Masculine and Feminine. Easy Import has separate toggles "Transfer To Face Meshes" (eyelashes, tears, brows and beards), "Transfer To Clothes", "Transfer To Geografts", "Transfer To Hair" and "Transfer To HD", and there is a manual Transfer Shapekeys tool. In Diffeomorphic's own vocabulary "ERC morphs" are Daz morphs that change the armature rest pose; these are ignored unless the global ERC Method setting (default: None) is changed, are only partially supported (Morph Armature / Auto Morph Armature, not updated during render), and are incompatible with IK rigs (MHX, Rigify).

claims.claim: As of 2026-09-15 (DAZ Importer 5.2.0, released August 2026), a Python script can drive the importer without the UI. The older route, documented by the developer in September-October 2024 and still functional but now marked deprecated in the source, is: resolve DAZ-relative paths with import_daz.get_absolute_paths([relpath]), pass the result to import_daz.set_selection(abspaths), call import_daz.set_silent_mode(True), then run bpy.ops.daz.easy_import_daz(useExpressions=..., useVisemes=..., useJcms=..., useMakePosable=...) (all four are real properties of that operator). With a legacy add-on install (Blender 4.1 and earlier, or a legacy install on later versions) the module is imported as import_daz; when installed as a Blender 4.2+ extension into Blender's default "User Default" repository it lives at bl_ext.user_default.import_daz, and the developer's example is `from bl_ext.user_default.import_daz import api` with a try/except ModuleNotFoundError fallback from `from import_daz import api`. Since version 4.4.0 (March 2025) the recommended way is to pass directory=... and files=[{"name": ...}] to easy_import_daz instead of calling set_selection. In silent mode errors are printed to the terminal instead of a pop-up dialog and the calling script is not blocked; the failing operator itself still aborts, and the script can inspect import_daz.get_error_message().

claims.claim: As of 2026-09-15: Diffeomorphic's preferred character path (Mesh Fitting "DBZ File (Characters)", the default) needs a .dbz file written by the add-on's "Export To Blender" script, run from Daz Studio's File menu. The .dbz is a gzipped JSON holding the final world-space (posed and morphed) vertex coordinates and bone data of each figure, plus optional HD mesh data (off by default); it does not store morph values. It is saved next to the .duf with the same name. Since 24 March 2021 a .duf can be imported without a .dbz using Mesh Fitting "Morphed (Characters)"; the feature appeared in the then-unreleased 1.6.0 development branch (1.6.0 was released on 28 August 2021) and was back-ported the same day to stable 1.5.1c. It costs extra manual steps: the wiki warns "Not all shapekeys are found" and "Shapekeys are not transferred to clothes", so shape keys must be transferred to clothes and hair (Transfer Shapekeys, called Transfer Other Morphs in 1.5.1) and applied, and characters defined through control morphs (CTRL files) need their FBM/FHM morphs loaded with "Import Custom Morph". Both routes require the Daz content library on disk and the same root paths set in the add-on as in Daz Studio; the no-dbz route only removes the need to run Daz Studio.

Relative DAZ references are resolved by GS.getAbsPath() against the plain Python lists GS.contentDirs + GS.mdlDirs + GS.cloudDirs, which a script can set with import_daz.set_global_setting('contentDirs', [...]) (a bare setattr on the GlobalSettings object, exceptions swallowed). That flag-driven standard-morph import does NOT use scan.py getMorphSet(); it takes its file lists from per-character tables in data/paths/*.json, which hard-code DAZ folder paths plus filename prefix/include rules. For Genesis 8 Female, for example, units and visemes (prefix "ectrlv") both come from data/DAZ 3D/Genesis 8/Female/Morphs/DAZ 3D/Base Pose Head/, expressions from .../DAZ 3D/Expressions/, facs (prefix "facs_") from .../Female 8_1/Morphs/Daz 3D/FACS/, facsexpr (prefix "facs_ctrl_") from .../Daz 3D/FACSExpressions/, and .../DAZ 3D/Base Pose/ is used for body morphs (prefix pctrl/ppbm); Genesis 9 facsdetails come from .../Daz 3D/FACS Details/. claims.claim: Blender 4.5 LTS works with Diffeomorphic 4.5.x/5.x but users reported a strong viewport regression in Blender 4.5 versus 4.2 (a Blender bug), which does not affect headless rendering.

Blender's Shader to RGB node is EEVEE-only: the node's own tooltip says "only supported in EEVEE", it is only offered in the Add menu when EEVEE is the active engine, and Cycles has no exporter for it, so in Cycles it is silently dropped. It is intended for non-photorealistic rendering, for example a colour ramp on the output of a Diffuse BSDF to make a toon shader. Per the Blender manual (4.5 through the 5.2 development branch, page text unchanged), using it "breaks the PBR pipeline", gives unpredictable results with ambient occlusion, contact shadows, soft shadows and screen-space refraction, and "doesn't give expected results in render passes" (it only works correctly in the Combined pass). Note that the manual page's warning that upstream BSDFs become invisible to "Screen Space Reflection, Subsurface Scattering, Alpha Clip and Alpha Hashed blend modes" is EEVEE Legacy wording from 2020 that was never updated: since Blender 4.2 (EEVEE Next) the Alpha Clip and Alpha Hashed blend modes no longer exist (Material > Blend Mode was replaced by Render Method: Dithered/Blended) and screen-space reflection is now the Raytracing > Screen-Trace method. For Blender 4.2 and later the manual's current description is that the node "evaluates the lighting of the BSDFs connected to it just like a Blended material and inherits its limitations", i.e. it is incompatible with render passes other than Combined and with ray tracing. (Verified 2026-09-15.)

As of 2026-09-15 (DSON spec v0.6.1.0): a DSON modifier may carry a morph (vertex_count plus a sparse float3_indexed_array of per-vertex deltas) or a skin_binding, never both, and may carry neither, in which case it is a pure channel used as formula input or output (this is how master switches such as Genesis 8's "JCMs On" are built). Modifiers, and also nodes, carry a formulas array. Each formula names one single-valued output property and an ordered RPN operation stack; the spec defines ten ops: push (a property url or literal val), add, sub, mult, div, inv, neg, spline_linear, spline_constant and spline_tcb (Kochanek-Bartels TCB, knot5 keys). Each formula has a stage, "sum" (default) or "multiply" in the spec text, and all formulas targeting the same property combine as (sum1+...+sumN) x mult1 x ... x multN. Files written by Daz Studio spell the multiply stage "mult", not "multiply", so a parser must accept both. This is the DSON encoding of Daz's ERC property links (DzERCLink: ERCDeltaAdd is push/push/mult, ERCKeyed is a spline op) and is how JCMs are driven from bone rotations: e.g. pJCMThighFwd_57_L.dsf pushes lThigh?rotation/x through spline_tcb into pJCMThighFwd_57_L?value, gated by a "mult"-stage formula that reads JCMs On?value.

claims.claim: As of 2026-09-15: Genesis 9's FACS morphs use Apple's ARKit vocabulary (facs_bs_EyeBlinkLeft, facs_bs_MouthSmileLeft, facs_bs_TongueOut, ...) but are not a byte-identical ARKit-52 set. The G9 Base FACS folder holds 285 morphs (161 facs_bs_, 99 facs_ctrl_, 25 facs_cbs_), and Daz splits many ARKit shapes into left/right or upper/lower components (facs_bs_CheekPuffLeft/Right; facs_bs_MouthCloseUpperLeft/UpperRight/LowerLeft/LowerRight; likewise MouthFunnel, MouthRoll, MouthShrug, MouthPress, BrowInnerUp) with a unipolar facs_ctrl_ driver on top (facs_ctrl_MouthClose drives the four MouthClose components, facs_ctrl_CheekPuff drives CheekPuffLeft/Right). Diffeomorphic's import table (data/facs/genesis9.json, 107 entries, last changed 2025-02-27) maps all 52 ARKit names onto this set: 20 of the 52 go to facs_ctrl_ controllers (browInnerUp, cheekPuff, mouthClose, mouthFunnel, mouthPucker, mouthRollUpper/Lower, mouthShrugUpper/Lower, mouthPressLeft/Right, eyeWideLeft/Right, all eight eyeLook*, jawForward, jawLeft/Right, mouthLeft/Right), and six of those take a -1 factor on a bipolar (-1..1) controller: eyeLookDownLeft/Right = facs_ctrl_EyeLookUp-DownLeft/Right x -1, eyeLookInRight and eyeLookOutLeft = facs_ctrl_EyeLookSide-SideRight/Left x -1, jawRight = facs_ctrl_JawLeft-Right x -1, mouthRight = facs_ctrl_MouthLeft-Right x -1; jawForward = facs_ctrl_JawForward-Recess x +1 (also bipolar, not a combined control). The sign flip is Diffeomorphic's routing choice, not a property of the Daz rig: G9 also ships direct unipolar (0..1) facs_bs_EyeLookDownLeft/Right, facs_bs_JawLeft/Right, facs_bs_MouthLeft/Right and facs_bs_JawForward/JawRecess, and Daz's own DazToRoblox mapping sends JawLeft/JawRight and MouthLeft/MouthRight straight to those. One further naming quirk: Diffeomorphic maps browDownLeft/Right and browOuterUpLeft/Right to facs_BrowDownLeft etc. (no bs_) because the modifier id inside facs_bs_BrowDownLeft.dsf really is facs_BrowDownLeft even though the file name and "name" field carry the bs_ prefix.

claims.claim: Exporting Genesis 9 with FBX morph rules 'Genesis9.facs_ctrl' and 'Genesis9.facs_bs' set to Export produces blend shapes that Unity's ARKit face mapper assigned automatically.

As of 2026-09-15 (sources span Daz Studio 4.10 to 4.24; the 4.24.0.3 and 6.x change logs record no change to FBX morph export), Daz Studio's FBX exporter chooses which morphs to write through 'Morph Export Rules' (the 'Edit Morph Export Rules' button in the FBX Export Options dialog). Each rule is a Match string, searched case-sensitively against morph names of the form node_name.parameter_name (sourced examples: 'FBMHeavy', '.eCTRLv', '.Z '), plus an Action of Bake, Export or Ignore; any morph no rule matches is Baked. Morphs set to Export arrive in the FBX as blend shapes, but FBX does not keep the ERC links between morphs and other properties, so exported JCMs do not fire automatically when the figure is posed. The 'Maya Helper Scripts' option (added in 4.10.0.122) reconnects them in Maya only; Daz's own bridges (e.g. Daz to Unreal) re-drive JCMs from 'JointLinks' data in their .dtu sidecar file, not from the FBX. HD morphs are not exported. Users report occasional 'very weird results' when exporting morphs on merged geometry. Exporting a full morph set without restrictive rules bloats the file; hair can exceed 2 GB, which yields an invalid FBX that will not open.
